"""Discharge a representation invariant at the callers that construct the type.

A representation invariant (RFC-0007 kind 1, #387) is *assumed* at entry of every
function that takes ``T *``. Nothing in that check says the callers that build a
``T`` hand over one that satisfies it, so an over-strong invariant can hide a bug.
This module closes the gap the way RFC-0003 S3 closes the memory-precondition one:
the assumption becomes an **obligation** asserted at the callee's entry in a
*generated copy* of the translation unit, and every caller in it is verified
against that copy.

What it generalises, and what it does not:

* The injection is S3's (`find_definition_brace`, same-line insertion so every line
  number matches the user's file, a ``#line`` directive for ``__FILE__``). The
  predicate is the invariant, ``{ const T *self = <param>; __ESBMC_assert(...); }``
  at the entry of each non-initialiser function with a ``T *`` parameter -- the
  functions the inductive check assumes it for. An initialiser (``rb_init``) is
  what *establishes* the invariant, so it receives no obligation.
* The caller sweep reuses `open_caller_checks`/`CallerCheck`/`CallerOutcome` and
  the same fail-closed aggregation: a clean sweep upgrades only for a ``static``
  callee (an externally visible one exports the obligation to other translation
  units), only when every caller was checked and passed, and only after a site
  probe shows the call is reached.
* A caller is **closed**: it takes no parameters of its own (``main``, a test
  driver), so it constructs the ``T`` it passes. A caller that takes parameters
  (including one that relays a ``T *`` it was handed) is not verified here --
  materialising those is a reachable context built by ``init`` (#127) -- and
  withholds the discharge, never claims it.

The caller's own ``assert()`` calls are compiled out (``NDEBUG``, set before the
user's includes): ESBMC reports one violated property per run, and a caller's own
assertion that the broken state trips first would hide the obligation behind it.
The question here is whether the invariant holds on entry, not whether the caller
is otherwise correct; the caller's own properties are its own unit's to check.

Results are *bounded*: a discharge is "VERIFIED up to k" for one invocation of each
caller from the translation unit's initial state, never "proof". An invariant that
is not discharged stays *assumed*, and says why.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import nullcontext
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import Enum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, assert_never

from forseti.esbmc import (
    ListUnitsError,
    Unit,
    Verified,
    Violated,
)
from forseti.esbmc.units import TranslationUnitAnalysis, analyze_translation_unit
from forseti.orchestrator.ladder import climb_to_terminal, validated_ladder
from forseti.orchestrator.ports import VerifyPort
from forseti.properties import Property
from forseti.properties.invariant import InvariantRole, infer_role

from .discharge import _self_reachable, open_caller_checks
from .model import CallerCheck, CallerOutcome
from .reachability import ProbeReachability, classify_site_probe
from .synth import RENAMED_MAIN, SynthError, _line_directive, find_definition_brace
from .synth import pointee_type as pointee_type

DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX = "forseti:rep-invariant-entry:"
DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX = "forseti:rep-invariant-site:"

_NDEBUG_PRELUDE = "#ifndef NDEBUG\n#define NDEBUG\n#endif\n"


class DischargeStatus(Enum):
    """What the callers of one invariant-assuming function established."""

    DISCHARGED = "discharged"  # every caller closed, reached, and satisfies it
    VIOLATED = "violated"  # a caller hands over a T the invariant does not hold on
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"  # a caller's run was inconclusive: nothing was settled
    INCOMPLETE = "incomplete"  # the caller set is open: the invariant stays assumed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvariantDischarge:
    """One invariant's discharge status at one function that assumes it."""

    property_id: str
    expression: str
    callee: str
    status: DischargeStatus
    detail: str
    callers: tuple[CallerCheck, ...] = ()
    k: int | None = None

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        """The honest one-word-plus-reason reading, never "proof"."""
        match self.status:
            case DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED:
                return f"DISCHARGED (VERIFIED up to k={self.k}): {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.VIOLATED:
                return f"VIOLATED: {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN:
                return f"UNKNOWN (still assumed): {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE:
                return f"ASSUMED (not discharged): {self.detail}"
            case _:
                assert_never(self.status)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "property_id": self.property_id,
            "expression": self.expression,
            "function": self.callee,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "discharged": self.status is DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
            "assumed": self.status is not DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
            "k": self.k,
            "detail": self.detail,
            "callers": [c.to_dict() for c in self.callers],
        }


DischargeOutcome = Literal["violated", "unknown", "incomplete", "empty", "discharged"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvariantDischargeRun:
    """Every stored invariant of one type, discharged function by function."""

    type_key: str
    discharges: tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]

    @property
    def outcome(self) -> DischargeOutcome:
        """Worst-outcome-wins: violated > unknown > incomplete > empty > discharged.

        ``empty`` (no invariant stored, or no function takes the type) is never
        read as a discharge.
        """
        statuses = {d.status for d in self.discharges}
        if DischargeStatus.VIOLATED in statuses:
            return "violated"
        if DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN in statuses:
            return "unknown"
        if DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE in statuses:
            return "incomplete"
        if not statuses:
            return "empty"
        return "discharged"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "type": self.type_key,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "discharges": [d.to_dict() for d in self.discharges],
        }


# The process status of `forseti invariant-discharge`. A discharge that stays
# `incomplete` is the *assumed* state every invariant already had, reported loudly
# (like S3's ASSUMED_VERIFIED, 0); `unknown` is a distinct non-zero state, never a
# silent pass.
DISCHARGE_EXIT_CODES: dict[DischargeOutcome, int] = {
    "discharged": 0,
    "incomplete": 0,
    "empty": 0,
    "violated": 1,
    "unknown": 2,
}


def assuming_functions(
    units: Sequence[Unit], type_name: str, initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
) -> tuple[tuple[Unit, tuple[str, ...]], ...]:
    """The functions that assume the invariant of `type_name`, with its parameters.

    A unit assumes it when a single-level ``T *`` / ``const T *`` parameter points
    to the type and the function is not an initialiser (`infer_role`, or named in
    `initialisers`): the same set the inductive check (`check --type`) assumes it
    for. Each is paired with the names of those parameters.
    """
    found: list[tuple[Unit, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
    for unit in units:
        if unit.name in initialisers or infer_role(unit.name) is InvariantRole.INITIALISER:
            continue
        names = tuple(
            p.name for p in unit.params if pointee_type(p.type) == type_name
        )
        if names:
            found.append((unit, names))
    return tuple(found)


def _entry_check(callee: str, param: str, type_name: str, expression: str) -> str:
    assertion = (
        f'__ESBMC_assert(({expression}), "{DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee}:{param}");'
    )
    if param == "self":
        return f"{{ {assertion} }}"
    return f"{{ const {type_name} *self = {param}; {assertion} }}"


def inject_invariant_obligation(
    source_text: str,
    callee: Unit,
    params: Sequence[str],
    *,
    type_name: str,
    expression: str,
    source_path: str,
    site_probe: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """`source_text` with the invariant asserted at `callee`'s entry.

    A **generated copy**: the user's file stays pristine. One block per parameter
    of `params` is inserted immediately after the definition's ``{`` on that same
    line, so every line number matches the original. A parameter itself named
    ``self`` is asserted over directly (aliasing it would initialise it from
    itself). With `site_probe` the obligation is replaced by one labelled
    ``assert(0)`` marking the entry, which a caller that reaches the call makes
    fail: the reachability reading that keeps a dead call site from discharging
    vacuously. ``NDEBUG`` and a ``#line`` restoring `source_path` are prepended
    without shifting any line. `SynthError` for an unnamed parameter or a
    definition that is not isolable.
    """
    if any(not name for name in params):
        raise SynthError(f"{callee.name}() has an unnamed {type_name} * parameter")
    brace = find_definition_brace(
        source_text, callee.name, callee.def_line, callee.predefined_guards
    )
    if brace is None:
        raise SynthError(f"no definition of {callee.name}() found in the source text")
    if site_probe:
        checks = [f'__ESBMC_assert(0, "{DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee.name}");']
    else:
        checks = [
            _entry_check(callee.name, name, type_name, expression.strip())
            for name in params
        ]
    injected = "".join(f" {check}" for check in checks)
    copy = source_text[: brace + 1] + injected + source_text[brace + 1 :]
    return _NDEBUG_PRELUDE + _line_directive(source_path) + copy


def render_caller_harness(copy_path: Path, caller: str) -> str:
    """A ``main`` that runs the closed `caller` once against the injected copy."""
    target = RENAMED_MAIN if caller == "main" else caller
    return (
        f"#define main {RENAMED_MAIN}\n"
        f'#include "{copy_path}"\n'
        "#undef main\n"
        "int main(void) {\n"
        f"    {target}();\n"
        "    return 0;\n"
        "}\n"
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Verify:
    port: VerifyPort
    ladder: tuple[int, ...]
    work_dir: Path


def _check_caller(
    caller: Unit,
    callee: Unit,
    obligations: Path,
    site: Path,
    run: _Verify,
) -> CallerCheck:
    """Verify `caller`'s one invocation against the obligation-injected copy."""
    if caller.params:
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
            "takes parameters, so it is not a closed caller that constructs the "
            "type itself; a caller that relays a pointer it was handed is "
            "covered only by its own inductive check, and a reachable context "
            "for its parameters needs `init` (#127)",
        )
    stem = f"{callee.name}__inv__{caller.name}"
    harness = run.work_dir / f"{stem}.c"
    harness.write_text(render_caller_harness(obligations, caller.name))
    settled = climb_to_terminal(harness, verify=run.port, ladder=run.ladder)
    result, k = settled.result, settled.k

    if isinstance(result, Violated):
        if f"{DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee.name}:" in result.raw_counterexample:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED,
                f"hands {callee.name}() a value the invariant does not hold on",
                k,
                result,
            )
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.CALLER_VIOLATED,
            "violates a property of its own (not the invariant) before the "
            "obligation is reached",
            k,
            result,
        )
    if not isinstance(result, Verified):
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
            f"inconclusive up to k={k} ({result.verdict.value})",
            k,
            result,
        )

    site_harness = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__site.c"
    site_harness.write_text(render_caller_harness(site, caller.name))
    probe = run.port(site_harness, unwind=k)
    match reading := classify_site_probe(probe, label=DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX):
        case ProbeReachability.REACHED:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.DISCHARGED,
                f"reaches {callee.name}() and the invariant holds on entry",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case ProbeReachability.UNREACHABLE:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNREACHABLE,
                f"never reaches {callee.name}(), so its pass discharges nothing",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case ProbeReachability.INCONCLUSIVE:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
                f"could not confirm {callee.name}() is reached "
                f"({probe.verdict.value})",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case _:
            assert_never(reading)


def _inconclusive(check: CallerCheck) -> bool:
    """A run that settled nothing: it faulted on its own, or ESBMC could not say."""
    return check.esbmc_result is not None and check.outcome in (
        CallerOutcome.CALLER_VIOLATED,
        CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
    )


def _aggregate(
    prop: Property,
    callee: Unit,
    checks: tuple[CallerCheck, ...],
    *,
    internal: bool,
) -> InvariantDischarge:
    """Fold the per-caller checks into one status, upgrading only on a clean sweep."""

    def result(
        status: DischargeStatus, detail: str, k: int | None = None
    ) -> InvariantDischarge:
        return InvariantDischarge(
            prop.property_id, prop.expression, callee.name, status, detail, checks, k
        )

    broken = tuple(c for c in checks if c.outcome is CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED)
    if broken:
        names = ", ".join(f"{c.caller}()" for c in broken)
        return result(
            DischargeStatus.VIOLATED,
            f"{names} hands {callee.name}() a value the invariant does not hold "
            "on at entry, so it is not established by what constructs it",
            max((c.settled_k or 0) for c in broken),
        )
    withheld = tuple(c for c in checks if c.outcome is not CallerOutcome.DISCHARGED)
    if withheld:
        why = "; ".join(f"{c.caller}(): {c.detail}" for c in withheld)
        status = (
            DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN
            if any(_inconclusive(c) for c in withheld)
            else DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE
        )
        return result(status, f"discharge incomplete: {why}")
    if not internal:
        return result(
            DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE,
            f"every caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit establishes "
            f"the invariant, but {callee.name}() is externally visible, so a "
            "client in another translation unit can call it with anything; the "
            "obligation is exported there, and closing it needs "
            f"{callee.name}() to be static or discharged in that unit too",
        )
    k = max((c.settled_k or 0) for c in checks)
    return result(
        DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
        f"every caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit is closed, "
        "reaches the call and establishes the invariant, for one invocation of "
        "each caller from this translation unit's initial state",
        k,
    )


def _discharge_function(
    prop: Property,
    callee: Unit,
    params: tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    type_name: str,
    source: Path,
    source_text: str,
    units: Sequence[Unit],
    open_callers_fn: Callable[[Path, str], tuple[CallerCheck, ...]],
    run: _Verify,
) -> InvariantDischarge:
    def incomplete(detail: str) -> InvariantDischarge:
        return InvariantDischarge(
            prop.property_id,
            prop.expression,
            callee.name,
            DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE,
            detail,
        )

    resolved = str(source.resolve())
    try:
        obligations = inject_invariant_obligation(
            source_text,
            callee,
            params,
            type_name=type_name,
            expression=prop.expression,
            source_path=resolved,
        )
        site = inject_invariant_obligation(
            source_text,
            callee,
            params,
            type_name=type_name,
            expression=prop.expression,
            source_path=resolved,
            site_probe=True,
        )
    except SynthError as exc:
        return incomplete(f"the obligation could not be injected: {exc}")
    try:
        unenumerable = open_callers_fn(source, callee.name)
    except ListUnitsError as exc:
        return incomplete(f"the caller set could not be enumerated: {exc}")

    referrers = tuple(
        u for u in units if u.name != callee.name and callee.name in u.calls
    )
    internal = any(u.internal_linkage for u in units if u.name == callee.name)
    if not referrers:
        detail = (
            f"no caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit, so the "
            "invariant is exported to its clients rather than discharged here"
        )
        if unenumerable:
            why = "; ".join(f"{c.caller}: {c.detail}" for c in unenumerable)
            detail = f"{detail}; the caller set is also open: {why}"
        return incomplete(detail)

    stem = f"{callee.name}__inv"
    obligations_path = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__obligations.c"
    obligations_path.write_text(obligations)
    site_path = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__obligation_site.c"
    site_path.write_text(site)

    checks = tuple(
        _check_caller(caller, callee, obligations_path, site_path, run)
        for caller in referrers
    )
    if _self_reachable(list(units), callee.name):
        # The assert fires at every entry, so one failing run cannot say whether a
        # caller's value or a re-entry the body made broke it: blaming the caller
        # would accuse code that handed over exactly what it built.
        checks = tuple(
            replace(
                c,
                outcome=CallerOutcome.UNATTRIBUTED,
                detail=f"{callee.name}() can re-enter itself and the obligation "
                "is asserted at every entry, so this failure cannot be "
                "attributed to this caller",
            )
            if c.outcome is CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED
            else c
            for c in checks
        ) + (
            CallerCheck(
                callee.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNATTRIBUTED,
                "re-enters itself, which this check does not explore from a "
                "caller's state",
            ),
        )
    return _aggregate(prop, callee, checks + unenumerable, internal=internal)


def discharge_invariants(
    source: Path,
    *,
    type_name: str,
    invariants: Sequence[Property],
    port: VerifyPort,
    ladder: tuple[int, ...],
    unwind: int,
    initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    work_dir: Path | None = None,
    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
    timeout_s: float = 30.0,
    list_units_fn: Callable[[Path], list[Unit]] | None = None,
    open_callers_fn: Callable[[Path, str], tuple[CallerCheck, ...]] | None = None,
) -> tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]:
    """Discharge each of `invariants` at every function of `type_name` that assumes it.

    `port` verifies a generated harness at a bound; `ladder` is the validated
    ``(unwind, *rungs)`` it climbs. With neither listing hook injected, unit
    planning and caller-completeness share one translation-unit AST (as
    `discharge_precondition` does). `ListUnitsError` propagates when the
    translation unit cannot be parsed at all.
    """
    if (list_units_fn is None) != (open_callers_fn is None):
        raise ValueError("inject both list_units_fn and open_callers_fn, or neither")
    if list_units_fn is None or open_callers_fn is None:
        analysis: TranslationUnitAnalysis = analyze_translation_unit(
            source, esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin, timeout_s=timeout_s
        )
        units = analysis.units()

        def open_callers(path: Path, symbol: str) -> tuple[CallerCheck, ...]:
            return open_caller_checks(symbol, path, analysis.caller_openings(symbol))
    else:
        units = list_units_fn(source)
        open_callers = open_callers_fn

    ladder = validated_ladder(unwind, ladder[1:] if ladder[:1] == (unwind,) else ladder)
    source_text = source.read_text()
    assuming = assuming_functions(units, type_name, initialisers)
    if not invariants or not assuming:
        return ()

    with (
        nullcontext(work_dir)
        if work_dir is not None
        else tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="forseti-invdischarge-")
    ) as directory:
        work = Path(directory)
        work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        run = _Verify(port, ladder, work)
        return tuple(
            _discharge_function(
                prop,
                callee,
                params,
                type_name=type_name,
                source=source,
                source_text=source_text,
                units=units,
                open_callers_fn=open_callers,
                run=run,
            )
            for prop in invariants
            for callee, params in assuming
        )


def invariant_discharge_transcript(run: InvariantDischargeRun) -> str:
    """Render a run as a readable transcript (pure, total).

    One line per (invariant, function), each led by its status so a discharged
    invariant is told apart from one that is still *assumed*, then a note on what
    the readings do and do not claim.
    """
    lines = [f"Forseti invariant discharge — {run.type_key}"]
    if not run.discharges:
        lines.append(
            "Nothing was discharged: no stored invariant, or no function of this "
            "file takes the type (the invariant stays assumed)."
        )
        return "\n".join(lines)
    by_property: dict[str, list[InvariantDischarge]] = {}
    for discharge in run.discharges:
        by_property.setdefault(discharge.property_id, []).append(discharge)
    for property_id, group in by_property.items():
        lines.append(f"Invariant {property_id}: {group[0].expression}")
        lines.extend(f"  {d.callee}(): {d.label}" for d in group)
        for d in group:
            lines.extend(
                f"    {c.caller}() [{c.outcome.value}]: {c.detail}" for c in d.callers
            )
    lines.append(
        "Note: a discharge is VERIFIED up to the bound k, for one invocation of "
        "each closed caller from this translation unit's initial state; the "
        "caller's own assert() calls are compiled out, so the verdict concerns "
        "the invariant only. Anything not DISCHARGED stays assumed."
    )
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Discharge a representation invariant at the callers that construct the type.

A representation invariant (RFC-0007 kind 1, #387) is *assumed* at entry of every
function that takes ``T *``. Nothing in that check says the callers that build a
``T`` hand over one that satisfies it, so an over-strong invariant can hide a bug.
This module closes the gap the way RFC-0003 S3 closes the memory-precondition one:
the assumption becomes an **obligation** asserted at the callee's entry in a
*generated copy* of the translation unit, and every caller in it is verified
against that copy.

What it generalises, and what it does not:

* The injection is S3's (`find_definition_brace`, same-line insertion so every line
  number matches the user's file, a ``#line`` directive for ``__FILE__``). The
  predicate is the invariant, ``{ const T *self = <param>; __ESBMC_assert(...); }``
  at the entry of each non-initialiser function with a ``T *`` parameter -- the
  functions the inductive check assumes it for. An initialiser (``rb_init``) is
  what *establishes* the invariant, so it receives no obligation.
* The caller sweep reuses `open_caller_checks`/`CallerCheck`/`CallerOutcome` and
  the same fail-closed aggregation: a clean sweep upgrades only for a ``static``
  callee (an externally visible one exports the obligation to other translation
  units), only when every caller was checked and passed, and only after a site
  probe shows the call is reached.
* A caller is **closed**: it takes no parameters of its own (``main``, a test
  driver), so it constructs the ``T`` it passes. A caller that takes parameters
  (including one that relays a ``T *`` it was handed) is not verified here --
  materialising those is a reachable context built by ``init`` (#127) -- and
  withholds the discharge, never claims it.

The caller's own ``assert()`` calls are compiled out (``NDEBUG``, set before the
user's includes): ESBMC reports one violated property per run, and a caller's own
assertion that the broken state trips first would hide the obligation behind it.
The question here is whether the invariant holds on entry, not whether the caller
is otherwise correct; the caller's own properties are its own unit's to check.

Results are *bounded*: a discharge is "VERIFIED up to k" for one invocation of each
caller from the translation unit's initial state, never "proof". An invariant that
is not discharged stays *assumed*, and says why.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import tempfile
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from contextlib import nullcontext
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from enum import Enum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Literal, assert_never

from forseti.esbmc import (
    ListUnitsError,
    Unit,
    Verified,
    Violated,
)
from forseti.esbmc.units import TranslationUnitAnalysis, analyze_translation_unit
from forseti.orchestrator.ladder import climb_to_terminal, validated_ladder
from forseti.orchestrator.ports import VerifyPort
from forseti.properties import Property
from forseti.properties.invariant import InvariantRole, infer_role

from .discharge import _self_reachable, open_caller_checks
from .model import CallerCheck, CallerOutcome
from .reachability import ProbeReachability, classify_site_probe
from .synth import RENAMED_MAIN, SynthError, _line_directive, find_definition_brace
from .synth import pointee_type as pointee_type

DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX = "forseti:rep-invariant-entry:"
DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX = "forseti:rep-invariant-site:"

_NDEBUG_PRELUDE = "#ifndef NDEBUG\n#define NDEBUG\n#endif\n"


class DischargeStatus(Enum):
    """What the callers of one invariant-assuming function established."""

    DISCHARGED = "discharged"  # every caller closed, reached, and satisfies it
    VIOLATED = "violated"  # a caller hands over a T the invariant does not hold on
    UNKNOWN = "unknown"  # a caller's run was inconclusive: nothing was settled
    INCOMPLETE = "incomplete"  # the caller set is open: the invariant stays assumed


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvariantDischarge:
    """One invariant's discharge status at one function that assumes it."""

    property_id: str
    expression: str
    callee: str
    status: DischargeStatus
    detail: str
    callers: tuple[CallerCheck, ...] = ()
    k: int | None = None

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        """The honest one-word-plus-reason reading, never "proof"."""
        match self.status:
            case DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED:
                return f"DISCHARGED (VERIFIED up to k={self.k}): {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.VIOLATED:
                return f"VIOLATED: {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN:
                return f"UNKNOWN (still assumed): {self.detail}"
            case DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE:
                return f"ASSUMED (not discharged): {self.detail}"
            case _:
                assert_never(self.status)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "property_id": self.property_id,
            "expression": self.expression,
            "function": self.callee,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "discharged": self.status is DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
            "assumed": self.status is not DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
            "k": self.k,
            "detail": self.detail,
            "callers": [c.to_dict() for c in self.callers],
        }


DischargeOutcome = Literal["violated", "unknown", "incomplete", "empty", "discharged"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InvariantDischargeRun:
    """Every stored invariant of one type, discharged function by function."""

    type_key: str
    discharges: tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]

    @property
    def outcome(self) -> DischargeOutcome:
        """Worst-outcome-wins: violated > unknown > incomplete > empty > discharged.

        ``empty`` (no invariant stored, or no function takes the type) is never
        read as a discharge.
        """
        statuses = {d.status for d in self.discharges}
        if DischargeStatus.VIOLATED in statuses:
            return "violated"
        if DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN in statuses:
            return "unknown"
        if DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE in statuses:
            return "incomplete"
        if not statuses:
            return "empty"
        return "discharged"

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "type": self.type_key,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "discharges": [d.to_dict() for d in self.discharges],
        }


# The process status of `forseti invariant-discharge`. A discharge that stays
# `incomplete` is the *assumed* state every invariant already had, reported loudly
# (like S3's ASSUMED_VERIFIED, 0); `unknown` is a distinct non-zero state, never a
# silent pass.
DISCHARGE_EXIT_CODES: dict[DischargeOutcome, int] = {
    "discharged": 0,
    "incomplete": 0,
    "empty": 0,
    "violated": 1,
    "unknown": 2,
}


def assuming_functions(
    units: Sequence[Unit], type_name: str, initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
) -> tuple[tuple[Unit, tuple[str, ...]], ...]:
    """The functions that assume the invariant of `type_name`, with its parameters.

    A unit assumes it when a single-level ``T *`` / ``const T *`` parameter points
    to the type and the function is not an initialiser (`infer_role`, or named in
    `initialisers`): the same set the inductive check (`check --type`) assumes it
    for. Each is paired with the names of those parameters.
    """
    found: list[tuple[Unit, tuple[str, ...]]] = []
    for unit in units:
        if unit.name in initialisers or infer_role(unit.name) is InvariantRole.INITIALISER:
            continue
        names = tuple(
            p.name for p in unit.params if pointee_type(p.type) == type_name
        )
        if names:
            found.append((unit, names))
    return tuple(found)


def _entry_check(callee: str, param: str, type_name: str, expression: str) -> str:
    assertion = (
        f'__ESBMC_assert(({expression}), "{DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee}:{param}");'
    )
    if param == "self":
        return f"{{ {assertion} }}"
    return f"{{ const {type_name} *self = {param}; {assertion} }}"


def inject_invariant_obligation(
    source_text: str,
    callee: Unit,
    params: Sequence[str],
    *,
    type_name: str,
    expression: str,
    source_path: str,
    site_probe: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """`source_text` with the invariant asserted at `callee`'s entry.

    A **generated copy**: the user's file stays pristine. One block per parameter
    of `params` is inserted immediately after the definition's ``{`` on that same
    line, so every line number matches the original. A parameter itself named
    ``self`` is asserted over directly (aliasing it would initialise it from
    itself). With `site_probe` the obligation is replaced by one labelled
    ``assert(0)`` marking the entry, which a caller that reaches the call makes
    fail: the reachability reading that keeps a dead call site from discharging
    vacuously. ``NDEBUG`` and a ``#line`` restoring `source_path` are prepended
    without shifting any line. `SynthError` for an unnamed parameter or a
    definition that is not isolable.
    """
    if any(not name for name in params):
        raise SynthError(f"{callee.name}() has an unnamed {type_name} * parameter")
    brace = find_definition_brace(
        source_text, callee.name, callee.def_line, callee.predefined_guards
    )
    if brace is None:
        raise SynthError(f"no definition of {callee.name}() found in the source text")
    if site_probe:
        checks = [f'__ESBMC_assert(0, "{DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee.name}");']
    else:
        checks = [
            _entry_check(callee.name, name, type_name, expression.strip())
            for name in params
        ]
    injected = "".join(f" {check}" for check in checks)
    copy = source_text[: brace + 1] + injected + source_text[brace + 1 :]
    return _NDEBUG_PRELUDE + _line_directive(source_path) + copy


def render_caller_harness(copy_path: Path, caller: str) -> str:
    """A ``main`` that runs the closed `caller` once against the injected copy."""
    target = RENAMED_MAIN if caller == "main" else caller
    return (
        f"#define main {RENAMED_MAIN}\n"
        f'#include "{copy_path}"\n'
        "#undef main\n"
        "int main(void) {\n"
        f"    {target}();\n"
        "    return 0;\n"
        "}\n"
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Verify:
    port: VerifyPort
    ladder: tuple[int, ...]
    work_dir: Path


def _check_caller(
    caller: Unit,
    callee: Unit,
    obligations: Path,
    site: Path,
    run: _Verify,
) -> CallerCheck:
    """Verify `caller`'s one invocation against the obligation-injected copy."""
    if caller.params:
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
            "takes parameters, so it is not a closed caller that constructs the "
            "type itself; a caller that relays a pointer it was handed is "
            "covered only by its own inductive check, and a reachable context "
            "for its parameters needs `init` (#127)",
        )
    stem = f"{callee.name}__inv__{caller.name}"
    harness = run.work_dir / f"{stem}.c"
    harness.write_text(render_caller_harness(obligations, caller.name))
    settled = climb_to_terminal(harness, verify=run.port, ladder=run.ladder)
    result, k = settled.result, settled.k

    if isinstance(result, Violated):
        if f"{DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX}{callee.name}:" in result.raw_counterexample:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED,
                f"hands {callee.name}() a value the invariant does not hold on",
                k,
                result,
            )
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.CALLER_VIOLATED,
            "violates a property of its own (not the invariant) before the "
            "obligation is reached",
            k,
            result,
        )
    if not isinstance(result, Verified):
        return CallerCheck(
            caller.name,
            CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
            f"inconclusive up to k={k} ({result.verdict.value})",
            k,
            result,
        )

    site_harness = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__site.c"
    site_harness.write_text(render_caller_harness(site, caller.name))
    probe = run.port(site_harness, unwind=k)
    match reading := classify_site_probe(probe, label=DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX):
        case ProbeReachability.REACHED:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.DISCHARGED,
                f"reaches {callee.name}() and the invariant holds on entry",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case ProbeReachability.UNREACHABLE:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNREACHABLE,
                f"never reaches {callee.name}(), so its pass discharges nothing",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case ProbeReachability.INCONCLUSIVE:
            return CallerCheck(
                caller.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
                f"could not confirm {callee.name}() is reached "
                f"({probe.verdict.value})",
                k,
                result,
            )
        case _:
            assert_never(reading)


def _inconclusive(check: CallerCheck) -> bool:
    """A run that settled nothing: it faulted on its own, or ESBMC could not say."""
    return check.esbmc_result is not None and check.outcome in (
        CallerOutcome.CALLER_VIOLATED,
        CallerOutcome.UNCHECKED,
    )


def _aggregate(
    prop: Property,
    callee: Unit,
    checks: tuple[CallerCheck, ...],
    *,
    internal: bool,
) -> InvariantDischarge:
    """Fold the per-caller checks into one status, upgrading only on a clean sweep."""

    def result(
        status: DischargeStatus, detail: str, k: int | None = None
    ) -> InvariantDischarge:
        return InvariantDischarge(
            prop.property_id, prop.expression, callee.name, status, detail, checks, k
        )

    broken = tuple(c for c in checks if c.outcome is CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED)
    if broken:
        names = ", ".join(f"{c.caller}()" for c in broken)
        return result(
            DischargeStatus.VIOLATED,
            f"{names} hands {callee.name}() a value the invariant does not hold "
            "on at entry, so it is not established by what constructs it",
            max((c.settled_k or 0) for c in broken),
        )
    withheld = tuple(c for c in checks if c.outcome is not CallerOutcome.DISCHARGED)
    if withheld:
        why = "; ".join(f"{c.caller}(): {c.detail}" for c in withheld)
        status = (
            DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN
            if any(_inconclusive(c) for c in withheld)
            else DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE
        )
        return result(status, f"discharge incomplete: {why}")
    if not internal:
        return result(
            DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE,
            f"every caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit establishes "
            f"the invariant, but {callee.name}() is externally visible, so a "
            "client in another translation unit can call it with anything; the "
            "obligation is exported there, and closing it needs "
            f"{callee.name}() to be static or discharged in that unit too",
        )
    k = max((c.settled_k or 0) for c in checks)
    return result(
        DischargeStatus.DISCHARGED,
        f"every caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit is closed, "
        "reaches the call and establishes the invariant, for one invocation of "
        "each caller from this translation unit's initial state",
        k,
    )


def _discharge_function(
    prop: Property,
    callee: Unit,
    params: tuple[str, ...],
    *,
    type_name: str,
    source: Path,
    source_text: str,
    units: Sequence[Unit],
    open_callers_fn: Callable[[Path, str], tuple[CallerCheck, ...]],
    run: _Verify,
) -> InvariantDischarge:
    def incomplete(detail: str) -> InvariantDischarge:
        return InvariantDischarge(
            prop.property_id,
            prop.expression,
            callee.name,
            DischargeStatus.INCOMPLETE,
            detail,
        )

    resolved = str(source.resolve())
    try:
        obligations = inject_invariant_obligation(
            source_text,
            callee,
            params,
            type_name=type_name,
            expression=prop.expression,
            source_path=resolved,
        )
        site = inject_invariant_obligation(
            source_text,
            callee,
            params,
            type_name=type_name,
            expression=prop.expression,
            source_path=resolved,
            site_probe=True,
        )
    except SynthError as exc:
        return incomplete(f"the obligation could not be injected: {exc}")
    try:
        unenumerable = open_callers_fn(source, callee.name)
    except ListUnitsError as exc:
        return incomplete(f"the caller set could not be enumerated: {exc}")

    referrers = tuple(
        u for u in units if u.name != callee.name and callee.name in u.calls
    )
    internal = any(u.internal_linkage for u in units if u.name == callee.name)
    if not referrers:
        detail = (
            f"no caller of {callee.name}() in this translation unit, so the "
            "invariant is exported to its clients rather than discharged here"
        )
        if unenumerable:
            why = "; ".join(f"{c.caller}: {c.detail}" for c in unenumerable)
            detail = f"{detail}; the caller set is also open: {why}"
        return incomplete(detail)

    stem = f"{callee.name}__inv"
    obligations_path = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__obligations.c"
    obligations_path.write_text(obligations)
    site_path = run.work_dir / f"{stem}__obligation_site.c"
    site_path.write_text(site)

    checks = tuple(
        _check_caller(caller, callee, obligations_path, site_path, run)
        for caller in referrers
    )
    if _self_reachable(list(units), callee.name):
        # The assert fires at every entry, so one failing run cannot say whether a
        # caller's value or a re-entry the body made broke it: blaming the caller
        # would accuse code that handed over exactly what it built.
        checks = tuple(
            replace(
                c,
                outcome=CallerOutcome.UNATTRIBUTED,
                detail=f"{callee.name}() can re-enter itself and the obligation "
                "is asserted at every entry, so this failure cannot be "
                "attributed to this caller",
            )
            if c.outcome is CallerOutcome.OBLIGATION_VIOLATED
            else c
            for c in checks
        ) + (
            CallerCheck(
                callee.name,
                CallerOutcome.UNATTRIBUTED,
                "re-enters itself, which this check does not explore from a "
                "caller's state",
            ),
        )
    return _aggregate(prop, callee, checks + unenumerable, internal=internal)


def discharge_invariants(
    source: Path,
    *,
    type_name: str,
    invariants: Sequence[Property],
    port: VerifyPort,
    ladder: tuple[int, ...],
    unwind: int,
    initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    work_dir: Path | None = None,
    esbmc_bin: str = "esbmc",
    timeout_s: float = 30.0,
    list_units_fn: Callable[[Path], list[Unit]] | None = None,
    open_callers_fn: Callable[[Path, str], tuple[CallerCheck, ...]] | None = None,
) -> tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]:
    """Discharge each of `invariants` at every function of `type_name` that assumes it.

    `port` verifies a generated harness at a bound; `ladder` is the validated
    ``(unwind, *rungs)`` it climbs. With neither listing hook injected, unit
    planning and caller-completeness share one translation-unit AST (as
    `discharge_precondition` does). `ListUnitsError` propagates when the
    translation unit cannot be parsed at all.
    """
    if (list_units_fn is None) != (open_callers_fn is None):
        raise ValueError("inject both list_units_fn and open_callers_fn, or neither")
    if list_units_fn is None or open_callers_fn is None:
        analysis: TranslationUnitAnalysis = analyze_translation_unit(
            source, esbmc_bin=esbmc_bin, timeout_s=timeout_s
        )
        units = analysis.units()

        def open_callers(path: Path, symbol: str) -> tuple[CallerCheck, ...]:
            return open_caller_checks(symbol, path, analysis.caller_openings(symbol))
    else:
        units = list_units_fn(source)
        open_callers = open_callers_fn

    ladder = validated_ladder(unwind, ladder[1:] if ladder[:1] == (unwind,) else ladder)
    source_text = source.read_text()
    assuming = assuming_functions(units, type_name, initialisers)
    if not invariants or not assuming:
        return ()

    with (
        nullcontext(work_dir)
        if work_dir is not None
        else tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="forseti-invdischarge-")
    ) as directory:
        work = Path(directory)
        work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        run = _Verify(port, ladder, work)
        return tuple(
            _discharge_function(
                prop,
                callee,
                params,
                type_name=type_name,
                source=source,
                source_text=source_text,
                units=units,
                open_callers_fn=open_callers,
                run=run,
            )
            for prop in invariants
            for callee, params in assuming
        )


def invariant_discharge_transcript(run: InvariantDischargeRun) -> str:
    """Render a run as a readable transcript (pure, total).

    One line per (invariant, function), each led by its status so a discharged
    invariant is told apart from one that is still *assumed*, then a note on what
    the readings do and do not claim.
    """
    lines = [f"Forseti invariant discharge — {run.type_key}"]
    if not run.discharges:
        lines.append(
            "Nothing was discharged: no stored invariant, or no function of this "
            "file takes the type (the invariant stays assumed)."
        )
        return "\n".join(lines)
    by_property: dict[str, list[InvariantDischarge]] = {}
    for discharge in run.discharges:
        by_property.setdefault(discharge.property_id, []).append(discharge)
    for property_id, group in by_property.items():
        lines.append(f"Invariant {property_id}: {group[0].expression}")
        lines.extend(f"  {d.callee}(): {d.label}" for d in group)
        for d in group:
            lines.extend(
                f"    {c.caller}() [{c.outcome.value}]: {c.detail}" for c in d.callers
            )
    lines.append(
        "Note: a discharge is VERIFIED up to the bound k, for one invocation of "
        "each closed caller from this translation unit's initial state; the "
        "caller's own assert() calls are compiled out, so the verdict concerns "
        "the invariant only. Anything not DISCHARGED stays assumed."
    )
    return "\n".join(lines)

def validated_ladder(unwind: int, unwind_ladder: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """`(unwind, *unwind_ladder)` after asserting strictly-increasing positive ints.

    The single source of truth for the ladder-shape rule (previously inline in
    `run_loop`): every rung must be >= 1 and each strictly greater than the last,
    so escalation always raises the bound. Raises `ValueError` otherwise.
    """
    ladder = (unwind, *unwind_ladder)
    if any(k < 1 for k in ladder) or any(b <= a for a, b in itertools.pairwise(ladder)):
        raise ValueError(
            f"unwind ladder must be increasing positive ints, got {ladder}"
        )
    return ladder


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LadderAttempt:
    """One rung of the ladder: the bound `k`, its verdict, and the escalation.

    `escalate_to` is the next bound the ladder will re-verify at *because* this
    rung's verdict was a non-terminal `Unknown`, or `None` when this attempt
    settles the ladder — a resolved (non-`Unknown`) verdict, or an `Unknown` at
    the final rung (exhausted, never a silent pass). It is the "will we escalate,
    and to what k" decision made data, so each driver reads it instead of
    re-deriving `ladder[position + 1]` for itself (the two can't drift).
    """

    k: int
    result: EsbmcResult
    escalate_to: int | None


def verify_ladder(
    source: Path, *, verify: VerifyPort, ladder: tuple[int, ...]
) -> Iterator[LadderAttempt]:
    """Verify `source` along `ladder`, escalating on `Unknown`.

    Verify at `ladder[0]`; on an `Unknown` verdict re-verify at the next rung,
    repeating until a non-`Unknown` verdict resolves it or the ladder is
    exhausted. Yields every attempt in order, one at a time *as it is computed*
    (at least one; the last is terminal), each carrying its own `escalate_to`
    decision: a caller emitting per attempt therefore flushes each completed rung
    — and its escalation — before the next verify is invoked, so a slow or
    interrupted later rung can't swallow an earlier verdict (issue #100). The
    escalation target is read from `ladder`, not by peeking at the next verify, so
    yielding stays lazy. When every rung is `Unknown` the final attempt is that
    terminal `Unknown` — the ladder is exhausted, never coerced to a pass.
    """
    for position, k in enumerate(ladder):
        result = verify(source, unwind=k)
        will_escalate = isinstance(result, Unknown) and position + 1 < len(ladder)
        escalate_to = ladder[position + 1] if will_escalate else None
        yield LadderAttempt(k, result, escalate_to)
        if not isinstance(result, Unknown):
            return

from forseti.esbmc import EXIT_CODES

from .check import check_source
from .invariant import (
    accepted_invariants,
    check_invariant_source,
    set_invariant_status,
    submit_invariant_source,
)
from .propose import propose_invariant_source, propose_source
from .submit import submit_source
from .verify import Payload, result_to_payload, verify_source

# The verdict->exit-code contract is owned by `forseti.esbmc` (the layer that
# owns `Verdict`) and re-exported here, so the unified `forseti` CLI and the
# low-level `forseti-esbmc` shell share one table and can never drift.

__all__ = [
    "EXIT_CODES",
    "Payload",
    "accepted_invariants",
    "check_invariant_source",
    "check_source",
    "propose_invariant_source",
    "propose_source",
    "result_to_payload",
    "set_invariant_status",
    "submit_invariant_source",
    "submit_source",
    "verify_source",
]
def _add_invariant_status_parser(
    sub: argparse._SubParsersAction[argparse.ArgumentParser],
) -> None:
    p = sub.add_parser(
        "invariant-status",
        help="accept or reject a stored representation invariant",
        description=(
            "Move one stored representation invariant of <source>::TYPE from "
            "candidate to accepted or rejected (both final; there is no grading "
            "step for an invariant). An accepted invariant is the context "
            "`forseti synth` assumes for every TYPE * function in <source>: it is "
            "*assumed* at entry, never discharged at the callers that construct "
            "TYPE, so an over-strong one can hide a bug. Accept it only after "
            "`forseti check --type TYPE` holds for the file's TYPE * functions. "
            "The property id is the one `submit-property` printed."
        ),
    )
    p.add_argument("source", type=Path, help="source file the invariant was stored for")
    p.add_argument(
        "--type",
        dest="type_name",
        required=True,
        metavar="TYPE",
        help="the struct type (ring_t or 'struct node') the invariant is over",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--property-id",
        required=True,
        metavar="ID",
        help="the invariant's property id",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "status",
        choices=("accepted", "rejected"),
        help="the status to move the invariant to",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--store-root",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT,
        metavar="DIR",
        help=f"the .forseti store directory (default: {DEFAULT_STORE_ROOT})",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--json", action="store_true", help="emit the updated invariant as JSON"
    )
    p.set_defaults(func=_run_invariant_status)


def _render_invariant_status(prop: Property, type_name: str) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"{prop.unit_id}: invariant {prop.property_id} is now "
        f"{prop.status.value.upper()}",
        f"  {prop.expression}",
    ]
    if prop.status is PropertyStatus.ACCEPTED:
        lines.append(
            f"`forseti synth` now assumes it for every {type_name} * function in "
            "this file (assumed, not discharged at the callers that construct it)."
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _run_invariant_status(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    try:
        prop = set_invariant_status(
            args.source,
            type_name=args.type_name,
            property_id=args.property_id,
            status=PropertyStatus(args.status),
            store_root=args.store_root,
        )
    except (PropertyStoreError, InvalidStatusTransition, OSError) as exc:
        print(f"forseti invariant-status: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(prop.to_dict()))
    else:
        print(_render_invariant_status(prop, args.type_name))
    return 0


def _add_grade_parser(
    sub: argparse._SubParsersAction[argparse.ArgumentParser],
) -> None:
    p = sub.add_parser(
        "grade",
        help="grade a unit's held properties by how many mutants they kill",
        description=(
            "Check <source>::<function>'s candidate properties on the real code, "
            "then re-check each held one against mutants of the function "
            "(equivalent mutants skipped). kill rate = killed / (killed + "
            "survived); unknown, error and skipped mutants are reported beside it, "
            "never folded in. Each graded property stores its kill rate and a "
            "reason naming every surviving mutant and becomes GRADED; a property "
            "with no killed or surviving mutant stays a candidate. Verdicts are "
            "bounded (up to k, len<=N), and skipping equivalent mutants by a "
            "bounded check inflates the kill rate. Exit 0 iff every held property "
            "was graded, 2 otherwise, 1 on a failed run."
        ),
    )
    _add_unit_store_arguments(p)

        "--max-mutants",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        metavar="N",
        help="grade against at most N valid mutants (a seeded sample; default: all)",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--seed",

"""Tests for `open_caller_checks` — the pure core of the openings seam (no ESBMC).

The five ways a callee's caller set can be *wider* than what `list_units` reports
(a header-defined caller, an address escape, an alias, a load-time attribute, a
GNU inline-asm call) each turn into a `CallerCheck` that withholds the discharge.
This is the `CallerOpenings`-in / `CallerCheck`s-out core: one place that owns
the taxonomy, testable directly without a translation unit, a filesystem, or
esbmc.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from forseti.esbmc import CallerOpenings, ListUnitsError

    defaults: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
        "foreign": (),
        "escaped": (),
        "aliased": (),
        "implicit": (),
        "asm_sites": (),
    }
    defaults.update(kw)
    return open_caller_checks("sum_bytes", SOURCE, CallerOpenings(**defaults))


def test_no_openings_is_empty() -> None:

"""Tests for `forseti.precond.invariant_discharge` (no ESBMC).

The injection is checked on text; the sweep through `discharge_invariants` with the
clang listing and the verifier both injected, dispatching on the generated
harness's filename so each phase (a caller's obligation run, its site probe) is
answered independently. The property under test is the same as S3's: a discharge
fails closed, and an invariant that is not discharged is reported as assumed.

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from forseti.esbmc import (

)

from forseti.precond.discharge import open_caller_checks
from forseti.precond.invariant_discharge import (

    DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX,
    DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX,
    DischargeStatus,
    InvariantDischarge,
    InvariantDischargeRun,

    discharge_invariants,
    inject_invariant_obligation,
    invariant_discharge_transcript,
    render_caller_harness,
)
from forseti.properties import Property, Provenance, make_invariant

INVARIANT = "self->count <= 4"
SOURCE = """\
typedef struct { unsigned count; } ring_t;

static void rb_init(ring_t *r) { r->count = 0; }
static int rb_push(ring_t *r, int v) { r->count++; return 1; }
static int rb_len(const ring_t *self) { return self->count; }
int main(void) {
    ring_t r;
    rb_init(&r);
    rb_push(&r, 1);
    return 0;
}
"""
RING = "ring_t *"


def _unit(
    name: str,
    params: tuple[Param, ...] = (),
    calls: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    *,
    internal: bool = True,
) -> Unit:
    return Unit(name, params, calls, internal_linkage=internal)


R = Param("r", RING)
INIT = _unit("rb_init", (R,))
PUSH = _unit("rb_push", (R, Param("v", "int")), calls=())
LEN = _unit("rb_len", (Param("self", "const ring_t *"),))
MAIN = _unit("main", (), ("rb_init", "rb_push", "rb_len"), internal=False)


def _meta() -> RunMeta:
    return RunMeta("8.6.0", ("esbmc",), 0, 0.0, "", "")


def _verified() -> Verified:
    return Verified(_meta())


def _violated(label: str = "") -> Violated:
    return Violated(_meta(), f"Violated property:\n  {label}", None)


def _property() -> Property:
    return make_invariant(
        type_key="x.c::ring_t",
        expression=INVARIANT,
        provenance=Provenance("p", "1", "hand", "human"),
    )


class Port:
    """A canned verifier: one answer per phase, a log of every file it was given."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        caller: EsbmcResult | None = None,
        site: EsbmcResult | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.caller = caller or _verified()
        self.site = site or _violated(DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, int]] = []

    def __call__(self, source: Path, /, *, unwind: int) -> EsbmcResult:
        self.calls.append((source.name, unwind))
        return self.site if source.name.endswith("__site.c") else self.caller


def _run(
    tmp_path: Path,
    port: Port,
    *,
    units: tuple[Unit, ...],
    callee_filter: str | None = None,
    openings: tuple[CallerCheck, ...] = (),
    initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    ladder: tuple[int, ...] = (),
) -> tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]:
    source = tmp_path / "x.c"
    source.write_text(SOURCE)
    results = discharge_invariants(
        source,
        type_name="ring_t",
        invariants=[_property()],
        port=port,
        unwind=4,
        unwind_ladder=ladder,
        initialisers=initialisers,
        work_dir=tmp_path / "work",
        list_units_fn=lambda _path: list(units),
        open_callers_fn=lambda _path, _symbol: openings,
    )
    if callee_filter is None:
        return results
    return tuple(r for r in results if r.callee == callee_filter)


def _push(tmp_path: Path, port: Port, **kw: object) -> InvariantDischarge:
    kw.setdefault("units", (INIT, PUSH, MAIN))

        return InvariantDischarge("id", "e", "f", status, "why")

    assert (

    assert outcome(DischargeStatus.UNKNOWN, DischargeStatus.VIOLATED) == "violated"

"""Tests for `forseti.precond.invariant_discharge` (no ESBMC).

The injection is checked on text; the sweep through `discharge_invariants` with the
clang listing and the verifier both injected, dispatching on the generated
harness's filename so each phase (a caller's obligation run, its site probe) is
answered independently. The property under test is the same as S3's: a discharge
fails closed, and an invariant that is not discharged is reported as assumed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from forseti.esbmc import (
    CallerOpenings,
    EsbmcResult,
    RunMeta,
    Unit,
    Unknown,
    UnknownReason,
    Verified,
    Violated,
)
from forseti.esbmc.units import Param
from forseti.precond import CallerCheck, CallerOutcome, SynthError
from forseti.precond.discharge import open_caller_checks
from forseti.precond.invariant_discharge import (
    DISCHARGE_EXIT_CODES,
    DISCHARGE_LABEL_PREFIX,
    DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX,
    DischargeStatus,
    InvariantDischarge,
    InvariantDischargeRun,
    assuming_functions,
    discharge_invariants,
    inject_invariant_obligation,
    invariant_discharge_transcript,
    render_caller_harness,
)
from forseti.properties import Property, Provenance, make_invariant

INVARIANT = "self->count <= 4"
SOURCE = """\
typedef struct { unsigned count; } ring_t;

static void rb_init(ring_t *r) { r->count = 0; }
static int rb_push(ring_t *r, int v) { r->count++; return 1; }
static int rb_len(const ring_t *self) { return self->count; }
int main(void) {
    ring_t r;
    rb_init(&r);
    rb_push(&r, 1);
    return 0;
}
"""
RING = "ring_t *"


def _unit(
    name: str,
    params: tuple[Param, ...] = (),
    calls: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    *,
    internal: bool = True,
) -> Unit:
    return Unit(name, params, calls, internal_linkage=internal)


R = Param("r", RING)
INIT = _unit("rb_init", (R,))
PUSH = _unit("rb_push", (R, Param("v", "int")), calls=())
LEN = _unit("rb_len", (Param("self", "const ring_t *"),))
MAIN = _unit("main", (), ("rb_init", "rb_push", "rb_len"), internal=False)


def _meta() -> RunMeta:
    return RunMeta("8.6.0", ("esbmc",), 0, 0.0, "", "")


def _verified() -> Verified:
    return Verified(_meta())


def _violated(label: str = "") -> Violated:
    return Violated(_meta(), f"Violated property:\n  {label}", None)


def _property() -> Property:
    return make_invariant(
        type_key="x.c::ring_t",
        expression=INVARIANT,
        provenance=Provenance("p", "1", "hand", "human"),
    )


class Port:
    """A canned verifier: one answer per phase, a log of every file it was given."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        caller: EsbmcResult | None = None,
        site: EsbmcResult | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.caller = caller or _verified()
        self.site = site or _violated(DISCHARGE_SITE_LABEL_PREFIX)
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, int]] = []

    def __call__(self, source: Path, /, *, unwind: int) -> EsbmcResult:
        self.calls.append((source.name, unwind))
        return self.site if source.name.endswith("__site.c") else self.caller


def _run(
    tmp_path: Path,
    port: Port,
    *,
    units: tuple[Unit, ...],
    callee_filter: str | None = None,
    openings: tuple[CallerCheck, ...] = (),
    initialisers: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
    ladder: tuple[int, ...] = (),
) -> tuple[InvariantDischarge, ...]:
    source = tmp_path / "x.c"
    source.write_text(SOURCE)
    results = discharge_invariants(
        source,
        type_name="ring_t",
        invariants=[_property()],
        port=port,
        unwind=4,
        unwind_ladder=ladder,
        initialisers=initialisers,
        work_dir=tmp_path / "work",
        list_units_fn=lambda _path: list(units),
        open_callers_fn=lambda _path, _symbol: openings,
    )
    if callee_filter is None:
        return results
    return tuple(r for r in results if r.callee == callee_filter)


def _push(tmp_path: Path, port: Port, **kw: object) -> InvariantDischarge:
    kw.setdefault("units", (INIT, PUSH, MAIN))
    (result,) = _run(tmp_path, port, callee_filter="rb_push", **kw)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    return result

"""End-to-end (real ESBMC): discharging the ring_t invariant at its callers (#430).

Drives `forseti invariant-discharge` on `examples/ring_buffer.c` and its staged-defect
twin. The constructing caller is the example's own `main`. Skipped when esbmc is not
on PATH.

* clean, correct invariant: `main` is checked at every call and passes, but the
  functions are externally visible, so the invariant stays *assumed* (exported);
* the same file with its functions made `static`: discharged;
* the staged defect: reported violated at `main`;
* an invariant the constructor does not establish (an over-strong one, or an
  `rb_init` that forgets a field): reported violated at `main`'s first call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from forseti.core.cli import main

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    shutil.which("esbmc") is None, reason="esbmc binary not on PATH"
)

EXAMPLES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "examples"
CLEAN = EXAMPLES / "ring_buffer.c"
BUG = EXAMPLES / "ring_buffer_bug.c"
INVARIANT = (
    "self->count <= CAP && self->head < CAP && self->tail < CAP "
    "&& (self->head + self->count) % CAP == self->tail"
)
OVER_STRONG = "self->count >= 1"


def _discharge(
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], source: Path, expression: str, root: Path
) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
    capsys.readouterr()
    code = main(
        [
            "submit-property",
            str(source),
            "--kind",
            "rep-invariant",
            "--type",
            "ring_t",
            "--expression",
            expression,
            "--provider",
            "hand",
            "--model",
            "human",
            "--store-root",
            str(root),
        ]
    )
    assert code == 0
    capsys.readouterr()
    code = main(
        [
            "invariant-discharge",
            str(source),
            "--type",
            "ring_t",
            "--store-root",
            str(root),
            "--json",
        ]
    )
    return code, json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)


def _by_function(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {entry["function"]: entry for entry in payload["discharges"]}


def _static_copy(tmp_path: Path, replacements: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> Path:
    text = CLEAN.read_text()
    for name in ("void rb_init", "int rb_push", "int rb_pop"):
        text = text.replace(f"\n{name}", f"\nstatic {name}")
    for old, new in (replacements or {}).items():
        assert old in text
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    path = tmp_path / "ring_static.c"
    path.write_text(text)
    return path


def test_clean_ring_buffer_is_checked_at_main_but_stays_assumed(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    code, payload = _discharge(capsys, CLEAN, INVARIANT, tmp_path / ".forseti")
    assert (code, payload["outcome"]) == (0, "incomplete")
    functions = _by_function(payload)
    assert set(functions) == {"rb_push", "rb_pop"}, "rb_init establishes, not assumes"
    for entry in functions.values():
        assert (entry["discharged"], entry["assumed"]) == (False, True)
        assert "externally visible" in entry["detail"]
        (caller,) = entry["callers"]
        assert (caller["caller"], caller["outcome"]) == ("main", "discharged")


def test_static_ring_buffer_is_discharged(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    source = _static_copy(tmp_path)
    code, payload = _discharge(capsys, source, INVARIANT, tmp_path / ".forseti")
    assert (code, payload["outcome"]) == (0, "discharged")
    for entry in payload["discharges"]:
        assert (entry["discharged"], entry["assumed"]) == (True, False)
        assert entry["k"] is not None


def test_the_staged_defect_is_violated_at_main(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    code, payload = _discharge(capsys, BUG, INVARIANT, tmp_path / ".forseti")
    assert (code, payload["outcome"]) == (1, "violated")
    for entry in payload["discharges"]:
        assert entry["status"] == "violated"
        (caller,) = entry["callers"]
        assert (caller["caller"], caller["outcome"]) == ("main", "obligation_violated")
        assert "forseti:rep-invariant-entry" in caller["counterexample"]


def test_an_invariant_the_constructor_does_not_establish_is_reported(
    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:

"""End-to-end (real ESBMC): discharging the ring_t invariant at its callers (#430).

Drives `forseti invariant-discharge` on `examples/ring_buffer.c` and its staged-defect
twin. The constructing caller is the example's own `main`. Skipped when esbmc is not
on PATH.

* clean, correct invariant: `main` is checked at every call and passes, but the
  functions are externally visible, so the invariant stays *assumed* (exported);
* the same file with its functions made `static`: discharged;
* the staged defect: reported violated at `main`;
* an invariant the constructor does not establish (an over-strong one, or an
  `rb_init` that forgets a field): reported violated at `main`'s first call.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

from forseti.core.cli import main

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    shutil.which("esbmc") is None, reason="esbmc binary not on PATH"
)

EXAMPLES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "examples"
CLEAN = EXAMPLES / "ring_buffer.c"
BUG = EXAMPLES / "ring_buffer_bug.c"
INVARIANT = (
    "self->count <= CAP && self->head < CAP && self->tail < CAP "
    "&& (self->head + self->count) % CAP == self->tail"
)
OVER_STRONG = "self->count >= 1"


def _discharge(
    capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], source: Path, expression: str, root: Path
) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
    capsys.readouterr()
    code = main(
        [
            "submit-property",
            str(source),
            "--kind",
            "rep-invariant",
            "--type",
            "ring_t",
            "--expression",
            expression,
            "--provider",
            "hand",
            "--model",
            "human",
            "--store-root",
            str(root),
        ]
    )
    assert code == 0
    capsys.readouterr()
    code = main(
        [
            "invariant-discharge",
            str(source),
            "--type",
            "ring_t",
            "--store-root",
            str(root),
            "--json",
        ]
    )
    return code, json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)


def _by_function(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    return {entry["function"]: entry for entry in payload["discharges"]}


def _static_copy(tmp_path: Path, replacements: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> Path:
    text = CLEAN.read_text()
    for name in ("void rb_init", "int rb_push", "int rb_pop"):
        text = text.replace(f"\n{name}", f"\nstatic {name}")
    for old, new in (replacements or {}).items():
        assert old in text
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    path = tmp_path / "ring_static.c"
    path.write_text(text)
    return path

    tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]

    assert (code, payload["outcome"]) == (0, "incomplete")
    functions = _by_function(payload)
    assert set(functions) == {"rb_push", "rb_pop"}, "rb_init establishes, not assumes"
    for entry in functions.values():

    # The dispatch contract: each registered subcommand carries its own handler
    # as a parser default, so `main` routes without a parallel name→function

        "codex-hook",

## Summary

Part of #3

An invariant is assumed at entry of every `T *` function (#387), and nothing checked that the callers that build a `T` establish it. This generalises RFC-0003 S3's injected obligation to representation invariants and adds `forseti invariant-discharge <src> --type T`.

- **Obligation.** For each stored (candidate or accepted) invariant of `T` and each non-initialiser function with a `T *` parameter (const included: the functions `check --type` assumes it for), `{ const T *self = p; __ESBMC_assert((inv), "forseti:rep-invariant-entry:fn:p"); }` is injected at the function's entry in a **generated copy** of the file, on the definition's own line (S3's `find_definition_brace` anchoring and `#line`), so line numbers match and the user's file is untouched. Initialisers (`init`/`initialise`/`initialize` name part, or `--initialiser NAME`) establish the invariant and receive none.
- **Sweep.** Reuses S3's `open_caller_checks` / `CallerCheck` / `CallerOutcome` and its fail-closed shape. Each caller is verified against the copy; a labelled `assert(0)` site probe shows the call is reached, so a dead call site discharges nothing. A caller must be **closed** (takes no parameters: `main`, a test driver). A caller with parameters, including one that relays a `T *`, is not verified here (a reachable context for those is #127) and withholds the discharge.
- **Status, per (invariant, function).** `discharged` (VERIFIED up to k) only when the function is `static`, every caller was closed, reached the call and passed, and the caller set is not open (escapes, aliases, asm). `violated` when a caller reaches the call in a state the invariant does not hold on. `unknown` when a run was inconclusive. Otherwise `incomplete`: the invariant stays *assumed* and says why (externally visible, no caller, caller takes parameters). JSON carries `discharged` and `assumed`. Exit: 0 discharged/incomplete/empty, 1 violated, 2 unknown.
- A function that can re-enter itself never blames its caller (`UNATTRIBUTED`), as in S3.

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).
